claim: Lunatic Fringe (Lfng) is expressed in the cochlea in Kölliker's organ with the Notch ligand Jag1 before the formation of the first inner hair cells.
source: Previous studies reported that Lunatic Fringe (Lfng) is expressed in the cochlea in Kölliker's organ with the Notch ligand Jag1 before the formation of the first inner hair cells (Morsli et al., 1998; Murata et al., 2006; Ohyama et al., 2010; Basch et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Morsli et al., 1998; Murata et al., 2006; Ohyama et al., 2010; Basch et al., 2011).

claim: As the first hair cell progenitors differentiate near the base of the cochlea, they express Atoh1 and Manic Fringe (Mfng).
source: As the first hair cell progenitors differentiate near the base of the cochlea, they express Atoh1 and Manic Fringe (Mfng; Cai et al., 2013, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Cai et al., 2013, 2015).

claim: Lfng and Mfng transiently co-localize at the site of Atoh1 expression at the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain.
source: We observed that Lfng and Mfng transiently co-localize at the site of Atoh1 expression at the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' observations from in situ hybridization experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Co-localization of Lfng and Mfng at the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain was confirmed by fluorescent in situ hybridization for Mfng in Lfng-GFP mice.
source: We confirmed this co-localization of Lfng and Mfng by performing fluorescent in situ hybridization for Mfng in Lfng-GFP mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: As hair cell and supporting cell differentiation continues, Lfng and Jag1 become restricted to supporting cells.
source: As hair cell and supporting cell differentiation continues, Fringe gene expression diverges once more, with Lfng and Jag1 becoming restricted to supporting cells (Morsli et al., 1998; Murata et al., 2006), and Mfng being restricted to hair cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Morsli et al., 1998; Murata et al., 2006).

claim: Mfng becomes restricted to hair cells as differentiation continues.
source: As hair cell and supporting cell differentiation continues, Fringe gene expression diverges once more, with Lfng and Jag1 becoming restricted to supporting cells (Morsli et al., 1998; Murata et al., 2006), and Mfng being restricted to hair cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' observations and a citation (Cai et al., 2015).

claim: Lfng-expressing cells at the prosensory domain border give rise to inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: In middle turn regions of the cochlea, we saw many EGFP-labeled inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells (Figure 2A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping experiments using Lfng-CreER transgenic mice crossed with Ai3 ROSA Cre reporter mice, with results shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Lfng;Mfng double mutant mice show significant numbers of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to controls (19.5 inner hair cells/100 µm compared to 12.3/100 µm in wild type controls).
source: In contrast, Lfng;Mfng double mutant mice showed significant numbers of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to controls (19.5 inner hair cells/100 µm compared to 12.3/100 µm in wild type controls; Figure 2C; Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from the authors' experiments shown in Figure 2C and Figure 3B.

claim: Lfng;Mfng double mutant mice show no significant changes in outer hair cell number (43.5 cells/100 µm versus 40.6 cells/100 µm in wild type controls).
source: In contrast, we observed no significant changes in outer hair cell number (43.5 cells/100 µm versus 40.6 cells/100 µm in wild type controls; Figure 2C; Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from the authors' experiments shown in Figure 2C and Figure 3C.

claim: Lfng mutant mice have no detectable cochlear phenotype.
source: Lfng mutant mice have previously been shown to have no detectable cochlear phenotype (Zhang et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Zhang et al., 2000).

claim: Mfng mutant mice have no cochlear phenotype.
source: Mfng mutant mice also had no cochlear phenotype (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Supernumerary inner hair cells in Lfng;Mfng mutants are accompanied by supernumerary inner phalangeal cells.
source: We found both markers continued to be expressed in Lfng;Mfng mutants, and that supernumerary inner phalangeal cells were found adjacent to supernumerary inner hair cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data for GLAST and FABP7 markers shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Loss of both Lfng and Mfng leads to a reduction in Notch signaling in the E15.5 cochlear duct.
source: We also confirmed that loss of both Lfng and Mfng led to a reduction in Notch signaling directly, by comparing N1ICD staining in Lfng;Mfng embryos to wild type controls (Figure 4A). In contrast to other regions of Lfng;Mfng mutant embryos such as the hindbrain (Figure 4A, inset), Lfng;Mfng mutants showed a reduction in N1ICD staining in the E15.5 cochlear duct.
evidence: The claim is supported by N1ICD immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Jag2 mutant mice display supernumerary inner hair cells.
source: Jag2 mutant mice display supernumerary inner hair cells (Lanford et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2000; Figure 3A,B), and we also observed supernumerary inner phalangeal cells in these mice on the basis of p27kip1, GLAST and FABP7 immunostaining (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Lanford et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2000) and data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Jag2 mutant mice display supernumerary inner phalangeal cells.
source: Jag2 mutant mice display supernumerary inner hair cells (Lanford et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2000; Figure 3A,B), and we also observed supernumerary inner phalangeal cells in these mice on the basis of p27kip1, GLAST and FABP7 immunostaining (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Jag1 heterozygous mice have increased inner hair cells.
source: Jag1 heterozygous mice also have increased inner hair cells (Kiernan et al., 2007; Moayedi et al., 2014), and we observed a similar phenotype of duplication of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells in Jag1 heterozygous mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Kiernan et al., 2007; Moayedi et al., 2014) and data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Jag1 heterozygous mice display duplication of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: Jag1 heterozygous mice also have increased inner hair cells (Kiernan et al., 2007; Moayedi et al., 2014), and we observed a similar phenotype of duplication of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells in Jag1 heterozygous mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Pofut1 conditional mutant mice exhibit supernumerary inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: Pofut1 conditional mutant mice also exhibited both supernumerary inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells (Figure 3A,B), suggesting that this phenotype can be caused by a general reduction in Notch signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: dnMAML1 mutant embryos display supernumerary inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: Embryos derived by mating Pax2-Cre and Cre-inducible dnMAML1 mice (Tu et al., 2005) also showed only a partial Notch loss of function (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B) and displayed both supernumerary inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Notch1 conditional null mutant mice show a very large increase in both inner and outer hair cells, and a great reduction of many kinds of supporting cells.
source: As expected, we observed a very large increase in both inner and outer hair cells, and a great reduction of many kinds of supporting cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Notch1 conditional mutants show no evidence for inner phalangeal cells on the basis of p27kip1, GLAST or FABP7 staining.
source: Significantly, we saw no evidence for inner phalangeal cells in Notch1 conditional mutants on the basis of p27kip1, GLAST or FABP7 staining (Figure 3A), suggesting that the cochlear phenotype caused by a strong Notch loss of function is due to a combination of an increase in inner hair / inner phalangeal progenitor specification and the subsequent differentiation of these ectopic progenitors exclusively into inner hair cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: No significant differences in EdU labeling were observed in outer hair cells, Deiters' cells, pillar cells, inner hair cells or inner phalangeal cells between wild type, Pofut1 and dnMAML1 conditional mutant mice.
source: We did not observe any significant differences in EdU labeling of outer hair cells, Deiters' cells, pillar cells, inner hair cells or inner phalangeal cells (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU incorporation data presented in Table 1.

claim: A modest but significant increase in EdU incorporation was observed in dnMAML1 border cells immediately adjacent to inner phalangeal cells (66 versus 59 labeled cells; p=0.014).
source: We observed a modest but significant increase in EdU incorporation in dnMAML1 border cells immediately adjacent to inner phalangeal cells (66 versus 59 labeled cells; p=0.014).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU incorporation data with statistical analysis.

claim: Doublets of Atoh1-expressing cells are consistently observed at the leading edge of hair cell differentiation in Pofut1 mutants, whereas single Atoh1-expressing cells are always observed in wild type cochleas.
source: We consistently observed doublets of Atoh1-expressing cells in this region of Pofut1 mutants, whereas single Atoh1-expressing cells were always observed at the leading edge of hair cell differentiation in wild type cochleas (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: At intermediate doses of DAPT or anti-Notch1 antibodies, a modest down-regulation of Hes1 and Hes5 is observed, but no significant down-regulation of Hey1, Hey2 or Heyl.
source: We observed a modest down-regulation of Hes1 and Hes5 at intermediate doses of DAPT or anti-Notch1 antibodies, but no significant down-regulation of Hey1, Hey2 or Heyl (Figure 5B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data from cultured cochleas shown in Figure 5B,E.

claim: At high concentrations of DAPT or anti-Notch1 antibodies, all Hes and Hey genes are significantly down-regulated with the exception of Hey2.
source: However, at high concentrations of either inhibitor, all genes were significantly down-regulated with the exception of Hey2, which is much less sensitive to changes in Notch signaling in the cochlea (Doetzlhofer et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data from cultured cochleas and a citation (Doetzlhofer et al., 2009).

claim: At high concentrations of DAPT or anti-Notch1 antibodies, significant increases in both outer and inner hair cells are observed, and a loss of inner phalangeal cells occurs.
source: At high concentrations of either inhibitor, we observed significant increases in both outer and inner hair cells, and a loss of inner phalangeal cells as revealed by the absence of GLAST-dsRed fluorescence (Figure 5A,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from cultured cochleas shown in Figure 5A,D.

claim: At 100-fold lower concentrations of Notch1 antibody or 25-fold lower doses of DAPT, a smaller but still significant increase in the number of inner hair cells is observed, but no significant increase in outer hair cell numbers.
source: In contrast, when we applied 100-fold lower concentrations of Notch1 antibody or 25-fold lower doses of DAPT to the cultures, we saw a smaller but still significant increase in the number of inner hair cells, but no significant increase in outer hair cell numbers (Figure 5C,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from cultured cochleas shown in Figure 5C,F.

claim: At intermediate doses of Notch inhibitors, GLAST-dsRed transgene expression continues to be observed, suggesting that inner phalangeal cells do not trans-differentiate into hair cells.
source: Moreover, we continued to observe expression of the GLAST-dsRed transgene at these doses (Figure 5A,D), suggesting that inner phalangeal cells do not trans-differentiate into hair cells, but remain adjacent to the supernumerary inner hair cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from cultured cochleas shown in Figure 5A,D and inference from the persistence of the marker.

claim: The organ of Corti contains mechanosensory inner and outer hair cells, surrounded by different types of supporting cells.
source: Its sensory organ, the organ of Corti, contains mechanosensory inner and outer hair cells, surrounded by different types of supporting cells (Kelley et al., 2009; Basch et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Kelley et al., 2009; Basch et al., 2016).

claim: The organ of Corti is bounded by two populations of non-sensory epithelium, the inner and outer sulci.
source: The organ of Corti is bounded by two populations of non-sensory epithelium, the inner and outer sulci.
evidence: The claim is based on established anatomical knowledge of the cochlea.

claim: High levels of BMP signaling promote outer sulcus differentiation.
source: High levels of BMP signaling promote outer sulcus differentiation, low or absent BMP signaling leads to formation of the inner sulcus, while intermediate levels of BMP signaling position the cochlear prosensory domain which will differentiate into the organ of Corti (Ohyama et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: Low or absent BMP signaling leads to formation of the inner sulcus.
source: High levels of BMP signaling promote outer sulcus differentiation, low or absent BMP signaling leads to formation of the inner sulcus, while intermediate levels of BMP signaling position the cochlear prosensory domain which will differentiate into the organ of Corti (Ohyama et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: Intermediate levels of BMP signaling position the cochlear prosensory domain which will differentiate into the organ of Corti.
source: High levels of BMP signaling promote outer sulcus differentiation, low or absent BMP signaling leads to formation of the inner sulcus, while intermediate levels of BMP signaling position the cochlear prosensory domain which will differentiate into the organ of Corti (Ohyama et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: Inner hair cells are the first cells to differentiate in the organ of Corti.
source: Inner hair cells, which are the first cells to differentiate in the organ of Corti, arise at the boundary of the prosensory domain and the future inner sulcus, also known as Kölliker's organ, in response to inducing signals (Groves and Fekete, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Groves and Fekete, 2012).

claim: Inner hair cells arise at the boundary of the prosensory domain and the future inner sulcus (Kölliker's organ) in response to inducing signals.
source: Inner hair cells, which are the first cells to differentiate in the organ of Corti, arise at the boundary of the prosensory domain and the future inner sulcus, also known as Kölliker's organ, in response to inducing signals (Groves and Fekete, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Groves and Fekete, 2012).

claim: The canonical Wnt signaling pathway promotes hair cell differentiation.
source: Recent work has identified several candidate signals that initiate hair cell development, including the canonical Wnt signaling pathway, that promote hair cell differentiation (Shi et al., 2010; Jacques et al., 2012; Shi et al., 2014; Jansson et al., 2015) and other signals, such as Shh, that hold hair cell differentiation in abeyance until they are down-regulated (Bok et al., 2013; Tateya et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Shi et al., 2010; Jacques et al., 2012; Shi et al., 2014; Jansson et al., 2015).

claim: Shh holds hair cell differentiation in abeyance until it is down-regulated.
source: Recent work has identified several candidate signals that initiate hair cell development, including the canonical Wnt signaling pathway, that promote hair cell differentiation (Shi et al., 2010; Jacques et al., 2012; Shi et al., 2014; Jansson et al., 2015) and other signals, such as Shh, that hold hair cell differentiation in abeyance until they are down-regulated (Bok et al., 2013; Tateya et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bok et al., 2013; Tateya et al., 2013).

claim: The Notch signaling pathway has been implicated in the establishment of boundaries between developmental territories.
source: The Notch signaling pathway has been implicated in the establishment of boundaries between developmental territories (Bray, 2006; Artavanis-Tsakonas and Muskavitch, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bray, 2006; Artavanis-Tsakonas and Muskavitch, 2010).

claim: A zone of Notch signaling is established between the dorsal and ventral halves of the Drosophila wing imaginal disc.
source: For example, a zone of Notch signaling is established between the dorsal and ventral halves of the Drosophila wing imaginal disc (Baker, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Baker, 2007).

claim: Fringe proteins modify Notch receptors and ligands to increase the level of Notch signaling by Delta ligands and to attenuate Notch signaling by Serrate ligands.
source: Fringe proteins modify Notch receptors and ligands to increase the level of Notch signaling by Delta ligands and to attenuate Notch signaling by Serrate ligands (Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).

claim: Fringe modification of Notch receptors tends to enhance signaling by Dll1 and Dll4 ligands and attenuate signaling by Jag1 and Jag2.
source: Current evidence suggests that Fringe modification of Notch receptors tends to enhance signaling by Dll1 and Dll4 ligands and attenuate signaling by Jag1 and Jag2 (Hicks et al., 2000; LeBon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hicks et al., 2000; LeBon et al., 2014).

claim: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands: Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2.
source: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands, Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2 (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015), of which Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands, whereas Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015).

claim: Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands.
source: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands, Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2 (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015), of which Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands, whereas Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell.
source: Differentiating hair cells express three Notch ligands, Dll1, Dll3 and Jag2 (Lanford et al., 1999; Morrison et al., 1999; Hartman et al., 2007; Maass et al., 2015), of which Dll1 and Jag2 act as conventional Notch ligands, whereas Dll3 appears to act only by inhibiting Notch receptors in the same cell (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Ladi et al., 2005; Geffers et al., 2007; Chapman et al., 2011).

claim: Notch signaling controls two sets of decisions at the edge of the organ of Corti.
source: We find Notch signaling controls two sets of decisions at the edge of the organ of Corti.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: The first decision restricts the first differentiating inner hair cells and their associated supporting cells, the inner phalangeal cells, to the boundary with Kölliker's organ.
source: The first decision restricts the first differentiating inner hair cells and their associated supporting cells, the inner phalangeal cells, to the boundary with Kölliker's organ.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: The first fate decision is regulated by Fringe activity, requires low levels of Notch signaling and is extremely sensitive to changes in signaling strength.
source: We find this fate decision is regulated by Fringe activity, requires low levels of Notch signaling and is extremely sensitive to changes in signaling strength.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: The second decision regulates the proportion of hair cells and supporting cells through lateral inhibition.
source: The second decision regulates the proportion of hair cells and supporting cells through previously characterized forms of lateral inhibition (Lewis, 1991, 1998; Kiernan, 2013).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings, interpretation, and citations to previous studies (Lewis, 1991, 1998; Kiernan, 2013).

claim: The second fate decision does not require Fringe activity, requires higher levels of Notch signaling, and is much less sensitive to small changes in signaling strength.
source: This fate decision does not require Fringe activity, requires higher levels of Notch signaling, and is much less sensitive to small changes in signaling strength.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: Qualitatively different forms of Notch signaling regulate different fate decisions during organ of Corti development.
source: Our results suggest that qualitatively different forms of Notch signaling regulate different fate decisions during organ of Corti development.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: Lfng and Mfng are transiently expressed precisely at the neural boundary of the organ of Corti.
source: We show that two Notch modifiers, Lfng and Mfng, are transiently expressed precisely at the neural boundary of the organ of Corti.
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The region where Lfng and Mfng are transiently expressed gives rise to inner hair cells and their associated inner phalangeal cells.
source: Cre-Lox fate mapping shows this region gives rise to inner hair cells and their associated inner phalangeal cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mutation of Lfng and Mfng disrupts the boundary of the organ of Corti, producing unexpected duplications of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: Mutation of Lfng and Mfng disrupts this boundary, producing unexpected duplications of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from Lfng;Mfng double mutant mice shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The duplication phenotype is mimicked by other mouse mutants or pharmacological treatments that lower but not abolish Notch signaling.
source: This phenotype is mimicked by other mouse mutants or pharmacological treatments that lower but not abolish Notch signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from multiple mutants and culture experiments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Strong disruption of Notch signaling generates many ectopic hair cells at the expense of inner phalangeal cells.
source: However, strong disruption of Notch signaling causes a very different result, generating many ectopic hair cells at the expense of inner phalangeal cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from Notch1 conditional mutants and high-dose inhibitor treatments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Notch signaling is finely calibrated in the cochlea to produce precisely tuned levels of signaling that first set the boundary of the organ of Corti and later regulate hair cell development.
source: Our results show that Notch signaling is finely calibrated in the cochlea to produce precisely tuned levels of signaling that first set the boundary of the organ of Corti and later regulate hair cell development.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental findings and interpretation.

claim: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that adds fucose moieties to Notch receptors and ligands.
source: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that adds fucose moieties to Notch receptors and ligands (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010), and whose activity generates the O-fucose substrate that is necessary for further N-glycosylation of Notch receptors by Fringe proteins (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010).

claim: Pofut1 activity generates the O-fucose substrate that is necessary for further N-glycosylation of Notch receptors by Fringe proteins.
source: Pofut1 is an O-fucosyltransferase that adds fucose moieties to Notch receptors and ligands (Takeuchi and Haltiwanger, 2010), and whose activity generates the O-fucose substrate that is necessary for further N-glycosylation of Notch receptors by Fringe proteins (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Shi et al., 2005).

claim: Pofut1 null mutant mice die between E9.5 and E10.5 with an axial phenotype reminiscent of a Notch loss of function.
source: Pofut1 null mutant mice die between E9.5 and E10.5 with an axial phenotype reminiscent of a Notch loss of function (Shi and Stanley, 2003), although different tissues can display differential sensitivities to loss of Pofut1 (Schuster-Gossler et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Shi and Stanley, 2003; Schuster-Gossler et al., 2009).

claim: Conditional deletion of Pofut1 in the cochlea with Pax2-Cre transgenic mice leads to a reduction, but not a complete loss of Notch signaling.
source: Conditional deletion of Pofut1 in the cochlea with Pax2-Cre transgenic mice leads to a reduction, but not a complete loss of Notch signaling, as revealed by the presence of cleaved Notch1-intracellular protein in the nuclei of Pofut1 mutant supporting cells and the enhancement of the Pofut1 mutant phenotype by additional Notch inhibition with gamma secretase inhibitors in organ culture (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and culture data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Loss of Lfng alone is able to rescue the inner hair cell phenotype, but not the outer hair cell phenotype of Jag2 mutant mice.
source: Our model can also explain why mutation of Lfng alone is able to rescue the inner hair cell phenotype, but not the outer hair cell phenotype of Jag2 mutant mice (Zhang et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Zhang et al., 2000).

claim: Loss of Lfng would partially relieve cis-inhibition of Dll1 expressed at the boundary and allow it to deliver more Notch signal to compensate for the loss of Jag2.
source: Since Lfng normally enhances cis-inhibition between Delta ligands and Notch receptors expressed in the same cell (LeBon et al., 2014), we predict that loss of Lfng would partially relieve cis-inhibition of Dll1 expressed at the boundary and allow it to deliver more Notch signal to compensate for the loss of Jag2.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the known function of Lfng and a citation (LeBon et al., 2014).

claim: An interaction between Lfng, Rfng and Mfng has been observed in the maturation of marginal zone B cell precursors.
source: However, an interaction between Lfng, Rfng and Mfng has been observed in the maturation of marginal zone B cell precursors (Tan et al., 2009; Song et al., 2016), suggesting that in at least some cases, the combined effects of these three enzymes on Notch signaling in either cis or trans cannot be achieved by either alone.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Tan et al., 2009; Song et al., 2016).

claim: A previous study described significant increases in proliferation in the progenitors of pillar cells, Deiters' cells and Hensen's cells in Dll1+/−;Jag2−/− and Dll1hyp/−;Jag2−/− mutant embryos, but not single mutants for either ligand.
source: A previous study described significant increases in proliferation in the progenitors of pillar cells, Deiters' cells and Hensen's cells in Dll1+/−;Jag2−/− and Dll1hyp/−;Jag2−/− mutant embryos, but not single mutants for either ligand (Kiernan et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kiernan et al., 2005).

claim: The strength of Notch signaling in vertebrates can vary according to both the identity and post-translational modification of the activated Notch receptor and the identity of the activating ligand.
source: It is now well established that the strength of Notch signaling in vertebrates can vary according to both the identity and post-translational modification of the activated Notch receptor and the identity of the activating ligand (for example, Ong et al., 2006; Yamamoto et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2013; Van de Walle et al., 2013; LeBon et al., 2014; Petrovic et al., 2014; Gama-Norton et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Hes5 mutant mice develop supernumerary inner hair cells and supporting cells at the onset of hair cell differentiation.
source: Furthermore, Hes5 mutant mice develop supernumerary inner hair cells and supporting cells at the onset of hair cell differentiation (Zine et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Zine et al., 2001).

claim: Inner hair cells release inducing signals such as Fgf8 that drive the differentiation of adjacent cells into pillar cells.
source: Our results provide additional evidence for the notion that organ of Corti development is an iterative process proceeding in the neural-abneural direction, with inner hair cells and their associated supporting cells differentiating first, which then release inducing signals such as Fgf8 that then drive the differentiation of the adjacent cells into pillar cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' findings and previous knowledge about Fgf8 function.

claim: When Notch ligands and receptors are present in the same cell, they attenuate each other's activity, a phenomenon known as cis-inhibition.
source: Previous studies suggest that when Notch ligands and receptors are present in the same cell, they attenuate each other's activity, a phenomenon known as cis-inhibition (del Alamo and Schweisguth, 2009; Becam et al., 2010; del Álamo et al., 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (del Alamo and Schweisguth, 2009; Becam et al., 2010; del Álamo et al., 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).

claim: Lfng and Mfng proteins increase cis-inhibition between Notch and Delta ligands, but decrease cis-inhibition between Notch and Jagged ligands.
source: Fringe proteins have been shown to modulate cis-inhibition: in vertebrates, Lfng and Mfng proteins increase cis-inhibition between Notch and Delta ligands, but decrease cis-inhibition between Notch and Jagged ligands (LeBon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (LeBon et al., 2014).

claim: The prosensory cell column adjacent to Kölliker's organ that expresses Jag1, Jag2, Dll1, Notch1, and Lfng and Mfng experiences cis-inhibition.
source: We therefore predict that the prosensory cell column adjacent to Kölliker's organ that expresses Jag1, Jag2, Dll1, Notch1, and Lfng and Mfng experiences cis-inhibition (Figure 6B, red inhibitory lines), leading to only a moderate amount of Notch signal delivered to Kölliker's organ.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from known Fringe function and the authors' model shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Loss of Lfng and Mfng is predicted to cause more cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Jag1 and Jag2, and less cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Dll1.
source: Loss of Lfng and Mfng is predicted to cause more cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Jag1 and Jag2, and less cis-inhibition between Notch1 and Dll1.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from known Fringe function.

claim: The entire column of cells at the boundary initially expresses early hair cell genes such as Atoh1 and Mfng.
source: Our current data, previous expression studies (Chen et al., 2002; Cai et al., 2013) and previous Atoh1 lineage tracing showing inner phalangeal cells derived from Atoh1-expressing cells (Yang et al., 2010) suggests this entire column of cells initially expresses early hair cell genes such as Atoh1 and Mfng.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' data and citations to previous studies (Chen et al., 2002; Cai et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2010).

claim: Moderate levels of Notch signaling have been visualized at the border of the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ in previous studies.
source: The moderate level of Notch signaling delivered at the border of the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ has been visualized in previous studies (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013; Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013) and data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Murata and colleagues have observed Atoh1-expressing cells adjacent to cells containing activated Notch1 at the boundary of Kölliker's organ.
source: Indeed, Murata and colleagues have observed Atoh1-expressing cells adjacent to cells containing activated Notch1 at the boundary of Kölliker's organ (Murata et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Murata et al., 2006).

claim: The duplication of inner phalangeal cells in previous Notch pathway mutant studies was not identified due to the lack of specific markers for these cells.
source: Although this phenotype can be observed in a number of previous studies in which Notch signaling was reduced or particular Notch ligands or Notch targets were mutated (Lanford et al., 1999; Zheng et al., 2000; Zine et al., 2001; Kiernan et al., 2005; Brooker et al., 2006; Tateya et al., 2011; Abdolazimi et al., 2016), the duplication of inner phalangeal cells in these studies was not identified due to the lack of specific markers for these cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the authors' findings and citations to previous studies.

claim: Jag1 is expressed in the cochlear duct as the first hair cells differentiate, and later in supporting cells.
source: The Jag1 ligand is also expressed in the cochlear duct as the first hair cells differentiate (Figure 1C), and later in supporting cells (Morrison et al., 1999; Woods et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and citations to previous studies (Morrison et al., 1999; Woods et al., 2004).

claim: GLAST and FABP7 are markers that label inner phalangeal cells.
source: To identify the type of supporting cells beneath the inner hair cells, we used antibodies to the glutamate/aspartate transporter GLAST encoded by the Slc1a3 gene and a nervous system-specific fatty acid binding protein, FABP7, both of which label inner phalangeal cells (Furness and Lehre, 1997; Saino-Saito et al., 2010; Zilberstein et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Furness and Lehre, 1997; Saino-Saito et al., 2010; Zilberstein et al., 2012).

claim: In the most apical regions of the cochlea, most EGFP-labeled cells from Lfng-CreER fate mapping are found in Kölliker's organ and very few in the inner hair cell region.
source: In the most apical regions of the cochlea, we observed most EGFP-labeled cells in Kölliker's organ and very few in the inner hair cell region (Figure 2A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with the expression of Lfng in this region between E12 and E14 (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and citations to previous studies (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: In basal regions of the cochlea from Lfng-CreER fate mapping, many labeled Deiters' cells, some labeled inner pillar cells as well as labeled inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells are observed.
source: In basal regions of the cochlea, we now observed many labeled Deiters' cells, some labeled inner pillar cells as well as labeled inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Lfng;Mfng;Rfng triple homozygous mutants show no significant difference in the number of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to Lfng;Mfng double mutant animals.
source: We were unable to detect expression of the third mammalian Fringe homologue, Radical Fringe (Rfng) in the cochlea, and Lfng;Mfng;Rfng triple homozygous mutants showed no significant difference in the number of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to Lfng;Mfng double mutant animals (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Radical Fringe (Rfng) expression was not detected in the cochlea.
source: We were unable to detect expression of the third mammalian Fringe homologue, Radical Fringe (Rfng) in the cochlea, and Lfng;Mfng;Rfng triple homozygous mutants showed no significant difference in the number of supernumerary inner hair cells compared to Lfng;Mfng double mutant animals (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' inability to detect Rfng expression.

claim: Only Jag2 mutants show a significant increase in outer hair cells among the mutants tested.
source: We found that Lfng;Mfng mutants, Jag2 mutants, Pofut1 conditional mutants and dMAML1 mutants all showed a significant increase in inner hair cells and the presence of extra inner phalangeal cells (Figure 3A,C), but we only observed an increase in outer hair cells in Jag2 mutants (Figure 3B; Lanford et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3B,C and a citation (Lanford et al., 1999).

claim: Notch1 conditional null mutant mice produce a significant loss of lateral inhibition between hair cells and supporting cells in the cochlea.
source: To test this, we examined Notch1 conditional null mutant mice which have been shown to produce a significant loss of lateral inhibition between hair cells and supporting cells in the cochlea (Kiernan et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kiernan et al., 2005).

claim: The cochlear phenotype caused by a strong Notch loss of function is due to a combination of an increase in inner hair/inner phalangeal progenitor specification and the subsequent differentiation of these ectopic progenitors exclusively into inner hair cells.
source: Significantly, we saw no evidence for inner phalangeal cells in Notch1 conditional mutants on the basis of p27kip1, GLAST or FABP7 staining (Figure 3A), suggesting that the cochlear phenotype caused by a strong Notch loss of function is due to a combination of an increase in inner hair / inner phalangeal progenitor specification and the subsequent differentiation of these ectopic progenitors exclusively into inner hair cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The supernumerary inner hair cells are induced at the same time as their normal counterparts when Notch signaling is reduced in the cochlea.
source: These results suggest that the supernumerary inner hair cells are induced at the same time as their normal counterparts when Notch signaling is reduced in the cochlea.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the Atoh1 expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The reduction in Notch signaling in Pofut1 and dnMAML1 mutants is insufficient to trigger aberrant proliferation.
source: We infer from this that the reduction in Notch signaling in all our Notch pathway mutants (with the exception of Notch1 conditional mutants) is insufficient to trigger aberrant proliferation, and that our phenotype is due solely to a disruption in the boundary between the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the EdU labeling data.

claim: The phenotype in Notch pathway mutants is due solely to a disruption in the boundary between the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
source: We infer from this that the reduction in Notch signaling in all our Notch pathway mutants (with the exception of Notch1 conditional mutants) is insufficient to trigger aberrant proliferation, and that our phenotype is due solely to a disruption in the boundary between the prosensory domain and Kölliker's organ.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the EdU labeling data and other experimental results.

claim: Hes5 promoter contains low-affinity Rbpj binding sites.
source: Indeed, low levels of Notch activation and Hes/Hey gene expression are observed at this boundary (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Tateya et al., 2011) and Hes5, whose promoter contains low-affinity Rbpj binding sites (Ong et al., 2006), is up-regulated at the boundary of Kölliker's organ as hair cells differentiate (Tateya et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Ong et al., 2006).

claim: Hes5 is up-regulated at the boundary of Kölliker's organ as hair cells differentiate.
source: Indeed, low levels of Notch activation and Hes/Hey gene expression are observed at this boundary (Murata et al., 2006; Basch et al., 2011; Tateya et al., 2011) and Hes5, whose promoter contains low-affinity Rbpj binding sites (Ong et al., 2006), is up-regulated at the boundary of Kölliker's organ as hair cells differentiate (Tateya et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Tateya et al., 2011).

claim: The Atoh1-GFP fusion protein is expressed a little later than Atoh1 mRNA.
source: The Atoh1-GFP fusion protein is expressed a little later than Atoh1 mRNA (Cai et al., 2013), but also provides a reliable indicator of differentiating hair cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Cai et al., 2013).

claim: Hair cell differentiation proceeds in a basal-apical direction over a period of several days.
source: Because hair cell differentiation proceeds in a basal-apical direction over a period of several days (Chen et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2006; Cai et al., 2013), we discuss the timing of these events with respect to the basal region of the cochlea (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Chen et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2006; Cai et al., 2013).

claim: Between E11 and E13, cells in the cochlear primordium express both Lfng and Jag1 in the presumptive Kölliker's organ and prosensory domain.
source: During the outgrowth of the cochlear duct, Jag1 and Lfng are expressed in cochlear progenitor cells (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Morsli et al., 1998; Ohyama et al., 2010).

claim: Lfng activity attenuates Jag1-Notch signaling between cells.
source: Lfng activity is known to attenuate Jag1-Notch signaling between cells (Hicks et al., 2000; Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014) which explains why these cochlear progenitor cells have been reported to receive low amounts of Notch signal (Figure 6A; Murata et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hicks et al., 2000; Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014).

claim: Cochlear progenitor cells expressing Jag1 and Lfng receive low amounts of Notch signal.
source: Lfng activity is known to attenuate Jag1-Notch signaling between cells (Hicks et al., 2000; Rana and Haltiwanger, 2011; LeBon et al., 2014) which explains why these cochlear progenitor cells have been reported to receive low amounts of Notch signal (Figure 6A; Murata et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Murata et al., 2006).

claim: Starting at approximately E13, the cochlear duct receives hair cell-inducing signals that reach a peak spanning the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain.
source: We propose that starting at approximately E13, the cochlear duct receives hair cell-inducing signals that reach a peak spanning the boundary of Kölliker's organ and the prosensory domain (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' model and interpretation of their data, shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A column of prosensory cells adjacent to Kölliker's organ begins to up-regulate early hair cell genes (Atoh1, Mfng, Jag2, Dll1) in response to hair cell-inducing signals.
source: In response to these hair cell-inducing signals, a column of prosensory cells adjacent to Kölliker's organ begins to up-regulate early hair cell genes (Atoh1, Mfng, Jag2, Dll1), while still maintaining expression of Notch1, Lfng and Jag1 (Figure 6B, green cell).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' model and data, shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The single column of differentiating hair cell progenitors sends Notch signals to its neighbors in Kölliker's organ that prevent them from responding to hair cell-inducing signals.
source: This single column of differentiating hair cell progenitors sends Notch signals to its neighbors in Kölliker's organ that prevent them from responding to hair cell-inducing signals (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' model and interpretation, shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The column of cells expressing Lfng, Mfng, Notch1, Atoh1, Dll1, Jag1 and Jag2 will ultimately form inner hair cells and their neighboring inner phalangeal cells.
source: Our Lfng-CreER fate mapping data show that this column of cells will ultimately form inner hair cells and their neighboring inner phalangeal cells (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The interaction between the column of differentiating hair cell progenitors and Kölliker's organ sets the boundary of the organ of Corti and establishes a single row of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: We suggest this interaction sets the boundary of the organ of Corti and establishes a single row of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' interpretation of their experimental findings.
